page: Amazon Web Services hpc6a.48xlarge is a high-performance computing instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and a 96-core AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at up to 3.6 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 96 physical cores without simultaneous multithreading (one thread per core), ensuring dedicated non-contended execution units for computational tasks. The instance includes 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and features a high-throughput 100 Gbps baseline network interface. It does not contain local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded computational and memory capabilities. The instance scores in the top tier (top 10%) across stress-ng multi-core tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and Clang compilation tests. Cached memory bandwidth reaches 12,154.54 GB/sec, while Redis SET operations achieved 179.29 million operations per second. However, single-threaded metrics, including Geekbench single-core and compression tests, remain in the average tier. Furthermore, without dedicated matrix accelerators such as AVX-512 or discrete GPUs, token generation performance on medium and large language models is significantly constrained.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high compute density per virtual machine boundary by dedicating 96 full AMD cores alongside 100 Gbps networking. The absence of integrated NVMe storage requires external network storage integration, but eliminates unnecessary local drive overhead for pure compute nodes. The hpc6a.48xlarge is primarily suited for tightly coupled high-performance computing workloads, computational fluid dynamics, finite element analysis, molecular dynamics, large-scale Clang or C++ compilation clusters, and parallel distributed batch processing.
description: Amazon Web Services hpc6a.48xlarge is a high-performance computing instance built on the Nitro system, featuring a dedicated 96-core AMD EPYC 7R13 processor clocked at 3.6 GHz. Operating without simultaneous multithreading, it delivers one physical core per vCPU alongside 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory and a 100 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes no local storage or discrete GPUs. In synthetic benchmarks, it achieves top-tier results in multi-core CPU stress tests, Clang compilation, ray tracing, and memory bandwidth, although single-threaded execution and GPU-dependent tasks like large model inference show standard or weak performance. The lack of integrated local storage directs the platform toward stateless or network-attached computing paradigms. hpc6a.48xlarge is structurally tailored for highly parallelized scientific simulations, computational engineering, batch processing, and distributed HPC workloads.
